audit.whatIsWrong: Level 2 was Skill and Level 6 was Neeko at 7/10, both against the packet chart (Neeko then Jax on every row) and against the mirror.
audit.why: The mirror moved rows 1 and 4 to Jax. My own whys[4] says his ultimate plus the Counter Strike stun eats the Pop Blossom wind-up, so row 4 was contradicting its own text, and a 46.15% win rate does not support Neeko owning the 6 spike.
audit.corrected: Row 1 -> Jax, row 4 -> Jax (7/10 -> 3/10), as matched full/content pairs in one group. Row 0 stays Neeko, which both the packet and the mirror agree on.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was rated Neeko's spike while the text says he leaps on the wind-up and shrugs the slam through his resist boost.
audit.why: Grandmaster-at-Arms gives armour and magic resist on activation, and Counter Strike's stun lands on a stationary Pop Blossom preparation. His level 6 is stronger than hers in this matchup.
audit.corrected: Row 4 moved to Jax; the spike text was already honest and stays.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four fields say Counter Strike dodges Neeko's root: early ('he can sit in your telegraphed E, dodge it'), whys[1], spikes[1].text and wants.foe[0].
audit.why: Riot's text is 'dodge all incoming attacks for a short duration' — basic attacks, not abilities. Blooming Burst and Tangle-Barbs land through Counter Strike; the only damage it removes is autos. The real threat is the stun at the end of the window, not a dodge on the root. The mirror caught the same error from Jax's side.
audit.corrected: early, whys[1], spikes[1].text and wants.foe[0] now say it dodges basic attacks and that the stun on expiry is what turns the trade.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid and wants.you[1] tell the player to bait Counter Strike using 'W (Shapesplitter) clone + invisibility'.
audit.why: Riot's Shapesplitter text is a third-attack proc plus a directional clone — there is no invisibility on it. The clone alone is the bait, and the concealment for the ult is the disguise, which Riot says hides the Pop Blossom preparation.
audit.corrected: mid and wants.you[1] rebuilt on the clone as bait and the disguise as concealment.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[5] and late both say his on-hit DPS deletes you 'once W and shields are down'. Neeko has no shield in her kit.
audit.why: Shapesplitter is a clone and a move speed proc; nothing in Neeko's kit absorbs damage. A player waiting for a shield to expire before disengaging is waiting on nothing.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten around stacked attack speed and the clone being spent.

audit.whatIsWrong: Counter Strike is the page's focus and the only number offered is dosFull[2].d's 'fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.why: It is 17/15/13/11/9s — 17 at rank 1, which is the longest punish window Neeko gets in this lane and the only period in which stepping up is safe.
audit.corrected: 17s written into dosFull[0].d, report[5].t, mid and wants.you[1].

edits.before: Jax takes E (Counter Strike) and can now dodge your telegraphed Tangle-Barbs and stun back — a missed root at melee is a free all-in for him.
edits.after: Jax takes Counter Strike: it dodges your autos, not your spells, but he holds it through the trade and stuns as it ends — a free all-in at melee.

edits.before: Jax's Trinity Force / BotRK spike turns the lane — his on-hit DPS deletes you once W and shields are down.
edits.after: Jax's Trinity Force / BotRK spike turns the lane — stacked attack speed deletes you inside one Counter Strike.

edits.before: Jax gets E (Counter Strike) — he can now dodge your E root and stun-back, so a whiffed Tangle-Barbs at melee is a free all-in for him.
edits.after: Jax gets Counter Strike — it dodges basic attacks, not Tangle-Barbs, but the stun at its end turns any melee-range trade into his all-in.

edits.before: Level 1 is your one clean window: Jax has no E (Counter Strike) yet, so throw Q (Blooming Burst) at him over the minions and land an E root if he steps up greedily for a cannon stack. The moment he hits 3 and has Counter Strike, everything changes — he can sit in your telegraphed E, dodge it, and stun you back, then Q-W gap-close for a trade you lose. Do not throw E at melee range hoping it lands; he just eats it. Farm with the edge of Q and respect that he wins any straight all-in once Counter Strike is up.
edits.after: Level 1 is your one clean window: Jax has no Counter Strike yet, so throw Q (Blooming Burst) at him over the minions and land an E root if he steps up greedily for a cannon stack. From level 3 everything changes — Counter Strike dodges basic attacks, so your spells still land, but he holds it through your trade and stuns you as it ends, then Q-W gap-closes. Never walk to melee to add autos; those are the only damage he actually dodges. Farm with the edge of Q and respect that he wins any straight all-in.

edits.before: Through 4-6 you can't commit without ult, and at 6 his R (Grandmaster's Might) plus the E dodge directly answers your Pop Blossom — if you channel it raw he leaps on you mid-wind-up and the stat boost shrugs your slam. The only way the combo lands is to bait his E first: use W (Shapesplitter) clone and invisibility to make him blow Counter Strike on nothing, THEN E-Q-R the real you. If his E is up, you don't have a kill. Use your Q waveclear to shove and roam instead — you're far better spent as a gank threat than feeding him stacks in a melee 1v1.
edits.after: Through 4-6 you can't commit without ult, and at 6 his R plus the Counter Strike stun directly answers your Pop Blossom — wind it up in the open and he leaps on you and shrugs the slam through his resist boost. The only way the combo lands is to bait the stun first: send the Shapesplitter clone so he burns Counter Strike on nothing, then E-Q-R from a disguise, where the preparation is hidden. Inside its 17 seconds you have a kill; outside them you have none. Otherwise shove with Q and roam — you're worth more as a gank threat than as stacks.

edits.before: Jax out-scales this lane outright: once his Trinity Force / Blade of the Ruined King and R stats come online, his on-hit DPS deletes your squishy body the instant W and your shields are down, and he survives your whole rotation. Do not try to splitpush into him or duel the side lane — he wins that every time. Group with your team where your AoE Pop Blossom and E root catch multiple targets, and let allies peel him off you. Convert any 6-and-first-item lead into objectives before the game goes long, because the longer it runs the more it's his.
edits.after: Jax out-scales this lane outright: once Trinity Force, Blade of the Ruined King and his ultimate's resists are online, stacked attack speed deletes your squishy body the moment your clone is spent, and he lives through your whole rotation. Do not splitpush into him or duel the side lane — he wins that every time. Group where your AoE Pop Blossom and E root catch multiple targets, and let allies peel him off you. Convert any early lead into objectives before the game goes long, because the longer it runs the more it's his.

edits.before: Use W (Shapesplitter) clone + invisibility to dodge his Q gap-close and bait his E Counter Strike empty
edits.after: Send the Shapesplitter (W) clone to bait his Counter Strike out empty, then commit inside that 17s

edits.before: Wait out your E root, then E (Counter Strike) your follow-up and Q-W gap-close onto you
edits.after: Hold Counter Strike through your whole trade, stun you as it ends, then Q-W gap-close onto you

edits.before: Dodges every auto and stuns — hold your damage until it ends. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Counter Strike dodges basic attacks and stuns, 17s at rank 1 — hold your autos through it, then commit.

edits.before: Track Jax’s Counter Strike: Dodges every auto and stuns — hold your damage until it ends. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Track Counter Strike: 17s at rank 1, it dodges basic attacks only and stuns at the end. It's down or you don't go.

notes: Name conflict I did not resolve unilaterally: the kit file (Data Dragon) calls Jax's R 'Grandmaster-at-Arms', but the mirror audit deliberately standardised this page's sister page on 'Grandmaster's Might' and lists that as a correction it made. The two pages will now read differently for the same ability. I left the existing 'Grandmaster's Might' text alone rather than introduce a mirror disagreement — see questionsForUser. Also worth flagging: the full layer's boilerplate ('Dodges every auto', 'Root the landing spot of Counter Strike') treats Counter Strike as a dash/engage, which it is not — his gap-close is Leap Strike (Q, 8s at rank 1). dosFull[0].t and dosFull[1].t are mislabelled in a way a per-string edit can't fix without rewriting the pair together.
